title: Classification
summary: Explain what classification predicts (a category) and build a simple classifier.
objectives: Tell classification (predicting a category) apart from regression (predicting a number)
Train a KNeighborsClassifier with n_neighbors=3 on a small labelled dataset
Predict the class of a new, unseen example
Explain a prediction with the nearest-neighbours idea

segments.title: What you will build
segments.body:
## What you will build

In the last lab the model predicted a number. A **classifier** predicts a category instead: spam or not spam, cat or dog, lemon, apple or mango. K-Nearest-Neighbours is the simplest classifier to picture: to label a new point it finds the K closest points in the training data and takes a majority vote. In this lab you will load `fruits.csv` (30 fictional fruits with their weight in grams, a sweetness score from 1 to 10 and their kind), train a `KNeighborsClassifier` with `n_neighbors=3`, and predict the kind of a new fruit that weighs 150 g with sweetness 6. You will then write one sentence that explains the answer using its three nearest neighbours.

lab.title: Which fruit is it? A 3-nearest-neighbours classifier
lab.objective: Train a KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=3) on weight and sweetness, predict the kind of a new fruit and explain the prediction.
lab.instructions:
The file fruits.csv has 30 rows with three columns: weight_g, sweetness (1 to 10) and fruit (lemon, apple or mango). The starter code already loads it into df.

1. Make X = df[["weight_g", "sweetness"]] (the two features) and y = df["fruit"] (the label).
2. Create model = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=3) and train it with model.fit(X, y).
3. new_fruit is a one-row table for a fruit of 150 g with sweetness 6. Store prediction = model.predict(new_fruit)[0] and print:
Prediction: <fruit>
4. Store one sentence (at least 8 words) in explanation that explains the prediction with the nearest-neighbours idea: name the predicted fruit and say that the 3 nearest neighbours of the new fruit in the data are that fruit, so the majority vote wins.

You can print(df.head()) while you work to see what the rows look like.
lab.constraints: Use KNeighborsClassifier from sklearn.neighbors with n_neighbors=3. Keep the names df, X, y, model, new_fruit, prediction and explanation. The prediction must come from model.predict, not be typed in by hand. No input().
lab.starter_code:
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier

df = pd.read_csv("fruits.csv")

# 1. X = the two feature columns weight_g and sweetness, y = the fruit column


# 2. model = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=3), then model.fit(X, y)


# 3. A new fruit: 150 g with sweetness 6. Predict its kind:
#    prediction = model.predict(new_fruit)[0]
#    Print:  Prediction: <fruit>
new_fruit = pd.DataFrame({"weight_g": [150], "sweetness": [6]})


# 4. One sentence (at least 8 words) explaining the prediction with the nearest-neighbours
#    idea: name the predicted fruit and its 3 nearest neighbours
explanation = ""
hints: X = df[["weight_g", "sweetness"]] picks the two feature columns and y = df["fruit"] the labels. A classifier learns from pairs of (features, label) exactly like the regression model did, but the label is a word, not a number.

model = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=3) and model.fit(X, y). model.predict(new_fruit) returns a list with one answer, so take [0] to get the fruit name as text: prediction = model.predict(new_fruit)[0].

Print with print("Prediction:", prediction). For the sentence, look at which fruits in the file are closest to 150 g and sweetness 6: explanation = "The 3 nearest neighbours of a 150 g fruit with sweetness 6 are apples, so the majority vote predicts apple."

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier

data = pd.DataFrame({"x": [0, 1, 0, 8, 9, 8], "y": [0, 0, 1, 8, 8, 9],
                     "label": ["left", "left", "left", "right", "right", "right"]})
model = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=3)
model.fit(data[["x", "y"]], data["label"])
print(model.predict(pd.DataFrame({"x": [2], "y": [1]}))[0])
print(model.predict(pd.DataFrame({"x": [7], "y": [9]}))[0])

lab.solution:
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier

df = pd.read_csv("fruits.csv")

X = df[["weight_g", "sweetness"]]
y = df["fruit"]

model = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=3)
model.fit(X, y)

new_fruit = pd.DataFrame({"weight_g": [150], "sweetness": [6]})
prediction = model.predict(new_fruit)[0]
print("Prediction:", prediction)

explanation = "The 3 nearest neighbours of a 150 g fruit with sweetness 6 are all apples, so the majority vote predicts apple."
